note: Both sets capture the four-column LIGHTING LEVELS table and the Title 24 switch/vacancy-sensor requirements, and both repeat roughly the same facts with and without conditions. Set A's values all match the page, whereas Set B introduces two clear misreads: General Use/Movement stated as 5 FC (page says 3 FC) and the CFL equivalent stated as 5W (text layer says 9W). Set A does omit the 40W incandescent = 9W CFL = 7W LED efficacy example that Set B partially captures, but Set B only gets the LED half of it right. On balance Set A is the more faithful set because it contains no wrong values.
remarks: Both sets duplicate nearly every table fact (with and without the activity condition) and use inconsistent attribute names ('lighting source' vs 'power source') for the same lamp-count row. Both quote the table header with typos ('CONRAST'/'CONSTRAC[T]'), which appear to be OCR/quote-layer artifacts rather than extraction errors. Both sets miss the statements that low-efficacy luminaires may be paired with vacancy sensors and dimmer switches, that dimmers vary energy consumption, and that the LED has higher efficacy because it emits more light per watt.
